triples.rationale: Malachi introduces the Lord's word delivered through His messenger; Haggai is explicitly called the Lord's messenger and speaks the Lord's assurance to the people. Both passages identify the messenger's speech as commissioned divine communication.
triples.source_text: A pronouncement of the word of the Lord concerning Israel through His messenger. Take it to your hearts!

target_units.text: Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the Lord their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him to them. The people feared before the Lord.
Haggai, the messenger of the Lord, said to the people, “I am with you, says the Lord.”

triples.rationale: Romans quotes the declaration that Jacob was loved and Esau hated. Malachi 1:2 supplies the first half of that contrast, which Romans places within its discussion of God's purpose concerning Isaac's children.
triples.source_text: “I have loved you,” says the Lord. But you said, “How hast Thou loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” says the Lord. “Yet I loved Jacob,

target_units.text: just as it is written, “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

triples.rationale: Malachi asks whether Esau was Jacob's brother. Genesis narrates their birth as twins and names Esau first and Jacob his brother, supplying the family relationship presupposed by the question.

target_units.text: And her days to give birth were fulfilled, and behold, there were twins in her womb.
And the firstborn son came out red, all over like a hairy hide; and he was named Esau.
And afterward his brother came out, and his hand held Esau’s heel; and he was named Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah bore them.

triples.rationale: Romans repeats the words about Esau being hated, completing the Jacob-Esau contrast begun in Malachi 1:2. The quotation concerns that declaration; it does not repeat Malachi's further description of Esau's desolated territories.
triples.source_text: but Esau I hated. I appointed his territories for desolation and his inheritance as gifts of a wilderness.”

triples.rationale: Malachi describes Esau's territories and inheritance as desolate wilderness. Isaiah's oracle, identified as judgment on Idumea in 34:5-6, likewise portrays deserted land and ruined fortifications occupied by wilderness creatures.
triples.source_text: but Esau I hated. I appointed his territories for desolation and his inheritance as gifts of a wilderness.”

target_units.text: Her ravines will turn to pitch, her earth to sulfur, and her land will burn like pitch
night and day. It will not be quenched for an everlasting time, and her smoke will rise upward. For generations and a long time she will be deserted.
Birds, hedgehogs, ibises and ravens will dwell in her; a measuring cord for deserted land will be cast upon her, and donkey-centaurs will dwell in her.
Her rulers will be no more, for her kings, her rulers and her magnates will come to destruction.
Thorny trees will sprout in their cities and her fortifications; she will become a dwelling for sirens and a courtyard for ostriches.

triples.rationale: Malachi says Idumea's rebuilding will be overthrown and describes enduring divine opposition. Obadiah announces the removal of understanding and warriors from Idumea and Mount Esau, ending with removal forever for violence toward Jacob.
triples.source_text: Because Idumea will say, “It has been overthrown; let us return and rebuild the deserted places,” thus says the Lord Almighty: “They will build, but I will overthrow. They will be called ‘Territories of Lawlessness’ and ‘A People Against Whom the Lord Has Drawn Up His Forces Forever.’”

target_units.text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.
Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,
because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.

triples.rationale: Malachi anticipates recognition that the Lord is magnified beyond Israel's territories. The psalm declares God King of all the earth, reigning over nations whose rulers gather with Abraham's God, expressing the same reach beyond Israel.
triples.source_text: Your eyes will see, and you yourselves will say, “The Lord has been magnified beyond Israel’s territories!”

target_units.text: For God is King of all the earth; make music with understanding.
God reigned over the nations; God sits upon His holy throne.
The rulers of peoples gathered with Abraham’s God; for the mighty of the earth belong to God; they were greatly exalted.

triples.rationale: Malachi's divine Father and Master asks for honor and fear from priests who belittle His name. Isaiah similarly indicts children who reject the God who raised them and contrasts Israel's failure with animals recognizing their owner and lord.
triples.source_text: “A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?” says the Lord Almighty. You priests who belittle My name! But you said, “How have we belittled Thy name?”

target_units.text: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”

triples.rationale: Malachi begins his accusation with the expectation that a son honors his father. Exodus explicitly commands honor for father and mother; Malachi uses that familiar filial duty as the premise for asking why God receives no honor as Father.
triples.source_text: “A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?” says the Lord Almighty. You priests who belittle My name! But you said, “How have we belittled Thy name?”

target_units.text: Honour your father and your mother, that it may be well with you, and that your days may be long upon the good land which the Lord your God gives you.

triples.rationale: Malachi accuses priests of bringing polluted food and despising the Lord's table. Leviticus instructs Aaron's sons to guard consecrated things and not profane God's name, excluding an unclean priest who approaches them.
triples.source_text: “By bringing polluted loaves to My altar.” But you said, “How have we polluted them?” “By your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is despised, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’”

target_units.text: Tell Aaron and his sons to exercise care concerning the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the Lord.

Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.

triples.rationale: Malachi condemns presenting blind or lame animals as sacrifices. Deuteronomy explicitly forbids sacrificing an animal with lameness, blindness or another grievous blemish, providing the rule violated by these offerings.
triples.source_text: “For if you bring a blind animal for sacrifice, is that not evil? If you bring one that is lame or sick, is that not evil? Bring it, then, to your ruler! Will he accept it? Will he show you favor?” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And if there is a blemish in it, lameness or blindness or any grievous blemish, you shall not sacrifice it unto the Lord your God.

triples.rationale: Malachi calls the offerers to plead with God while questioning whether their deeds will receive favor. Isaiah says multiplied supplication will not be heard from bloodstained hands and calls for cleansing and removal of evil deeds.
triples.source_text: “And now appease the face of your God and plead with Him. These things have happened in your hands. Will I show favor to any of you?” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.

triples.rationale: Malachi declares that God has no desire for the offerers and will not accept their sacrifice. Amos likewise rejects festivals, burnt offerings and sacrifices and refuses to hear their music, showing divine rejection of outward worship.
triples.source_text: “For even among you doors will be shut, and you will not kindle My altar for nothing. I have no desire for you,” says the Lord Almighty, “and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.”

target_units.text: “I have hated and rejected your festivals, and I certainly will not smell a pleasing scent in your festal gatherings,
because even if you bring Me whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not receive them, and I will not look upon the salvation offering of your display.
Remove from Me the sound of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your instruments,

triples.rationale: Malachi locates the glorifying of God's name from sunrise to sunset and among nations. The psalm uses the same span from the sun's risings to settings to praise the Lord's name and declares Him high above all nations.
triples.source_text: “For from the sun’s rising to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to My name, together with a pure sacrifice, because My name is great among the nations,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: From the sun’s risings to its settings, praise the name of the Lord.
The Lord is high above all nations; His glory is above the heavens.

triples.rationale: Malachi speaks of a pure sacrifice and the greatness of God's name among nations. Isaiah describes foreigners loving the Lord's name and bringing acceptable sacrifices to His altar in a house of prayer for all nations.
triples.source_text: “For from the sun’s rising to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to My name, together with a pure sacrifice, because My name is great among the nations,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And the foreigners attached to the Lord, to serve Him and love the Lord’s name, to become His male and female slaves, and all those keeping My Sabbaths from profanation and holding fast to My covenant—

I will bring them into My holy mountain and make them rejoice in My house of prayer. Their whole burnt offerings and sacrifices will be acceptable on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations,”

triples.rationale: Both verses repeat the priests' statement that the Lord's table and its food are despised. The repetition connects the charge of profaning in 1:12 with the polluted offerings already identified in 1:7.
triples.source_text: “But you profane it by your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is polluted, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’

target_units.text: “By bringing polluted loaves to My altar.” But you said, “How have we polluted them?” “By your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is despised, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’”

triples.rationale: Malachi includes goods seized by force among the unacceptable offerings. Sirach calls sacrifice from unjust gain a blemished offering and condemns sacrificing the property of the poor, explaining why wrongful acquisition cannot become an acceptable gift.
triples.source_text: “And you said, ‘These things are from hardship,’ and I blew them away,” says the Lord Almighty. “You were bringing things seized by force, the lame and the afflicted. If you bring the sacrifice, shall I accept these things from your hands?” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: One who sacrifices from unjust gain makes a blemished offering, and the gifts of the lawless bring no acceptance.
The Most High takes no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, nor does He atone for sins through a multitude of sacrifices.
The one who presents a sacrifice from the property of the poor is slaughtering a son before his father.

triples.rationale: Malachi curses the person who has a male pledged by a vow but sacrifices a damaged animal. Leviticus requires acceptable males without blemish for pledged offerings and insists that a sacrifice fulfilling a vow be unblemished.
triples.source_text: “Cursed is one who was able, and had a male in his flock and a vow concerning it, yet sacrifices a damaged animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the Lord Almighty, “and My name is manifest among the nations.”

target_units.text: Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto them in Israel, who presents his gifts according to any of their pledges or any of their freewill offerings, which they present unto God for a whole burnt offering,
to be acceptable for you, they shall be males without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.

And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.

triples.rationale: The command in 2:1 is expressly directed to priests. The earlier accusation in 1:6 names the priests who belittle God's name, identifying the group whose conduct the following command addresses.
triples.source_text: “And now this command is for you, priests.

target_units.text: “A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?” says the Lord Almighty. You priests who belittle My name! But you said, “How have we belittled Thy name?”

triples.rationale: Malachi threatens a curse upon the priests and their blessing if they refuse to listen and honor God's name. Deuteronomy likewise makes failure to listen and obey the trigger for curses that reach the people's stores, produce and work.
triples.source_text: If you do not listen and do not take it into your hearts to give glory to My name,” says the Lord Almighty, “I will send out the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessing, and I will curse it. I will scatter your blessing, and it will not be among you, because you do not take it into your hearts.

target_units.text: And it shall be, if you do not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that all these curses shall come upon you, and overtake you.
Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
Cursed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Cursed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Cursed are you when you go out, and cursed are you when you come in.

The Lord send upon you want, and famine, and wasting, in all that you put your hand unto, whatsoever you do, until He destroys you, and causes you to perish speedily, because of your evil practices, because you have forsaken Me.

triples.rationale: Malachi's threat names the shoulder and the stomach of the festivals, with the stomach scattered on the priests' faces. Deuteronomy assigns the foreleg and stomach among the priests' sacrificial portions; familiar priestly portions become instruments of humiliation in Malachi.
triples.source_text: Look, I am setting apart the shoulder for you, and I will scatter the stomach on your faces, the stomach of your festivals, and I will take you to the same place.

target_units.text: And this shall be the priests’ due from the people, from them that sacrifice a sacrifice, whether a calf or a sheep: they shall give unto the priest the foreleg, and the cheeks, and the stomach.

triples.rationale: Malachi says the command serves God's covenant with the Levites. Moses' blessing of Levi praises keeping God's oracles and covenant and assigns declaration of the law and service at the altar, setting out that covenantal responsibility.
triples.source_text: You will recognize that I have sent out this command to you, so that My covenant might be with the Levites,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And unto Levi he said, Give unto Levi his manifestations, and his truth unto the holy man, whom they tested in a trial, and reviled at the water of dispute;
who says unto his father and his mother, I have not seen you; and he did not acknowledge his brethren, and disowned his sons. He kept Thine oracles, and preserved Thy covenant.
They shall declare Thine ordinances unto Jacob, and Thy law unto Israel; they shall lay incense in Thy wrath, continually upon Thine altar.

triples.rationale: Malachi describes the priestly covenant as life and peace, received in reverence. Numbers explicitly grants Phinehas a covenant of peace and an enduring priesthood for his zeal, a particular priestly covenant corresponding to Malachi's description.
triples.source_text: “My covenant with him was of life and peace, and I gave it to him in fear, to fear Me and to shrink back before My name.

target_units.text: Therefore say: Behold, I give him a covenant of peace.
And it shall be for him and his seed after him an everlasting covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.

triples.rationale: Malachi's faithful priest carries true law in his mouth and turns people from injustice. Deuteronomy assigns Levi the task of declaring God's ordinances and law to Jacob and Israel, the teaching responsibility faithfully exercised in Malachi.
triples.source_text: A law of truth was in his mouth, and injustice was not found on his lips. Directing his way in peace, he walked with Me and turned many back from injustice.

target_units.text: They shall declare Thine ordinances unto Jacob, and Thy law unto Israel; they shall lay incense in Thy wrath, continually upon Thine altar.

triples.rationale: Malachi says a priest's lips guard knowledge and that people seek law from his mouth. Leviticus requires Aaron's priests to distinguish holy from profane and instruct Israel in the statutes delivered through Moses.
triples.source_text: For a priest’s lips will guard knowledge, and people will seek law from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

triples.rationale: Malachi describes people seeking law from a priest. Deuteronomy directs difficult legal questions to the Levitical priests and requires obedience to the judgment and law they declare, giving a concrete setting for that consultation.
triples.source_text: For a priest’s lips will guard knowledge, and people will seek law from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And if a matter in judgment is too hard for you, between blood and blood, and between judgment and judgment, and between injury and injury, and between dispute and dispute, matters of judgment within your cities, you shall arise and go up unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
And you shall come unto the Levitical priests, and unto the judge who shall be in those days; and they shall inquire, and declare unto you the judgment.

And you shall do according to the matter which they declare unto you from the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there; and you shall take diligent heed to do according to all that is laid down for you as law.
You shall do according to the law and according to the judgment which they tell you; you shall not turn aside from the word which they declare unto you, to the right hand or to the left.
